phase.label: Last years, President of the Board of Rites (1630s)

source.label: Sirén (citing the Wusheng shi shi): in the Chongzhen reign (1628–44) he was made president of the Board of Rites
Waley: Dong “completely identifies the Learned Man's Painting with the Southern School”
Sirén: Dong sought “the spirit of the old masters”

highlight.text: …however easy it may be to make a close copy, it is [difficult to] transmit the spirit.
highlight.lead: Mo Shilong, in words Dong also copied into his own writings:

source.author: Mo Shilong (Mo Shih-lung)
source.title: Writings on painting
source.publisher: translated in Osvald Sirén, Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (Lund Humphries, 1958; Internet Archive scan)

work.text: …one can hardly do better than pay some [attention] to one or several of the albums in which Tung united sets of ten or more studies after various old masters. … it is not [the] characteristics of the old masters which prevail, but those of their interpreter.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (The Later Ming and Leading Ch‘ing Masters)

work.text: The [brushwork] of Ching and Kuan … is full of life. [I] follow them without necessarily imitating them
work.lead: Dong, inscribing a leaf of another album after tenth-century masters:

source.author: Dong Qichang (Tung Ch‘i-ch‘ang)
source.title: Writings on painting
source.publisher: translated in Osvald Sirén, Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (Lund Humphries, 1958; Internet Archive scan)

moment.text: The prime essential is that the painter should imitate the Old Masters. After that he may go on to the imitation of natural objects.

source.author: Dong Qichang (Tung Ch‘i-ch‘ang)
source.title: Writings on painting
source.publisher: translated in Arthur Waley, An Introduction to the Study of Chinese Painting (Ernest Benn, 1923; Internet Archive scan)

moment.text: He could look upon new religions with a friendly and interested eye, but as regards painting his formalism and conservatism knew no bounds

source.author: Arthur Waley
source.title: An Introduction to the Study of Chinese Painting

matters.text: He has not copied them [but] absorbed them in, his own creative [consciousness], giving fresh life to their thoughts through this faculty [of absorption] and exceptional command of the [brush].

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (The Later Ming and Leading Ch‘ing Masters)
